- The reclining cat spreads across the middle-left to upper-right, with his head in the upper-right quadrant, centered approximately (72%,31%). His entire ears, face and chest are inside the frame. Face/ears occupy roughly 32% canvas width, not a giant close-up. Warmly expressive eyes remain a focus.

- The red calamity card hangs just below that paw at about (33%,76%). The COMPLETE rotated card fits within approximately x19%–45%, y63%–91%. Its total height is about 28% of the image height and width about 22% of image width. IMPORTANT: its entire bottom corner must end ABOVE 93% of the image height, leaving clear padding above the future title ribbon. Still make it plausibly suspended off the wooden table edge; no floating loose unrelated card. Keep the lightning and shattered tower pictogram and gold border.
- The tabletop front edge crosses diagonally from (0%,53%) to (100%,79%), passing directly under the reaching paw. The hanging card projects in front of the dark carved wooden table face. The tabletop perspective and the contact between paw/card/edge should clearly communicate pushing the card off.

- The trader's left hand near the left edge around 50%–64% height, coins nearby; right foreground hand holding green-and-gold cards near the lower-right around 62%–88% height. Those supporting hands are smaller than in the original and leave breathing room around the cat's gesture. Crop sleeves naturally at outer edges if necessary.
Keep all important subjects 6% away from outer edges for parallax, and reserve the very bottom 5% as uncomplicated dark table wood. More lateral environmental space and balanced nearly-square storytelling; not huge empty space. Preserve warm saturated lighting, bold clean polygonal planes, rich orange/teal contrast, and the same established cat. No frame or typography of any kind, no title banner, no rules panel, no extra characters. Full opaque illustration, suitable for later separation into foreground/center/background.
